utility.notes: Xcel Energy's list of Colorado communities served, dated 10/2015, shows Lafayette with gas and electricity service. The list names communities, not individual addresses. The City's New Solar PV checklist asks for an approved PV service application from Xcel Energy, and the City's Energy page says solar garden subscribers receive a credit on their Xcel bill. The City's pages do not name the electric utility for every address or give an address lookup. Check the utility named on your electric bill before you apply.

value.name: Xcel Energy
value.notes: Applies to addresses served by Xcel Energy; check your electric bill. Under Xcel net metering, any excess is held in a virtual bank to be applied against future bills.

permit_authority.notes: The Building Division reviews building permit applications, issues building permits, performs building inspections, issues contractor's licenses, enforces building codes and maintains building records. The City's solar checklist gives the City of Lafayette Planning & Building Department, 1290 S. Public Rd, Lafayette, Colorado 80026, as the contact. A building permit is required to install new electrical systems or to make additions, alterations or replacements to existing systems. The City's building pages do not say how to confirm that an address is inside city limits. For questions on whether you need a permit, the City says to call the Building Department at 303-661-1451.

permit_url.notes: All New Solar PV permit application materials must be submitted electronically. The City's Apply for Building Permits page says applicants must create an account in the Online Service Portal before submitting an application. The City's New Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Permit Application Checklist (2026) lists the required materials. Projects that require revisions can be resubmitted through the Online Service Portal. Access to the City's old MyGov system will end at the end of December 2026.

interconnection_url.notes: This applies if Xcel Energy is your electric utility; check your electric bill. Xcel says that in most cases the developer or installer submits the interconnection application on your behalf, or you can manage your own. The City's solar checklist lists an approved PV service application from Xcel Energy among the electrical plan requirements for the City permit. Xcel highly recommends that construction of your system should not start until your application receives full approval from the Xcel Energy engineering team and all final agreements are fully signed. The process ends with a permission to operate letter from Xcel to the generator owner. Xcel's permission to operate is a separate approval from the City permit and the City's inspections.

value.name: Renewable Battery Connect
value.description: Xcel says that when you add an eligible solar charged battery to your home or small business and participate, Xcel can automatically manage your battery during periods of peak demand on the grid (load control events). Upfront incentive, General: $250 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to $5,000 per application). Income Qualified: $1,000 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). Disproportionately Impacted Community: $500 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). There is also a $100 annual participation incentive for all customer types for participating in control events (for 5 years).
value.eligibility: An Xcel Energy program for a home or small business that adds an eligible solar charged battery. Xcel says eligible equipment includes all Tesla Powerwall models or all current Enphase models. Check that Xcel is your electric utility first.

battery_programs.notes: Xcel's page shows a 2026 General incentive budget with $10,635,423 available, on figures dated 11/02/2026. The City's Energy page says Switch Together Boulder County also offers deals on battery storage.

required_documents.notes: Lists are taken from the City's New Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Permit Application Checklist (2026). The checklist has more plan set items than are shown here, so prepare plans from the checklist itself. Incomplete submittals will not be accepted and may delay your review time. For resubmittals, the checklist asks for a complete set of revised plans and a written response to all department comments in one PDF.

value: If Xcel Energy is your utility, your installer usually submits the interconnection application to Xcel. The City's checklist requires an approved PV service application from Xcel Energy with the permit application.
Submit the permit application and plans electronically through the City's Online Service Portal.
Pay the permit fees, which are due when the permit is issued.
Schedule each inspection through the Online Service Portal by 3pm for the next business day. Requesting inspections is the responsibility of the contractor or homeowner.
Building Rough inspection (required when structural changes are made to the roof trusses or rafters).
For Xcel customers: after the interconnection is approved and all contracts are signed, Xcel works with you and your contractors to witness test and energize the system.
Xcel sends a permission to operate letter to the generator owner.
inspection_steps.notes: The required inspections are as listed in the City's New Solar PV checklist. City stamped plans must be onsite for all inspections, along with the building inspection record card. All inspections occur between 9am and 4pm, and you can call the Building Department at 303-661-1451 between 8 and 9am for your arrival time window. Someone over the age of 18 must be at the project address to provide access. The inspector signs the front of the permit card when an inspection is approved, and the inspections are needed to receive final approval for your project. Xcel highly recommends that construction should not start until your interconnection application receives full approval and all final agreements are fully signed. The City permit, the City's final approval and Xcel's permission to operate are separate approvals.

timeline_days.notes: The City's Apply for Building Permits page gives no processing time for solar permits. Solar is excluded from the Quick Permits category, which has an estimated processing time of 2 business days.

value.program_or_pathway: New Solar PV permit, submitted electronically through the Online Service Portal
other_conditions: Solar is excluded from the City's Quick Permits, and the online quick permit option is not for permits that require a plan review.
All contractors doing construction work within the City limits and being compensated for that work must be licensed with the City.
An Electrical Contractor License requires a copy of the State Master License and State Contractor License, has no fee, and is good for one year from the day it is issued.

A homeowner may obtain a building permit to work on their own property without a contractor's license unless the property is a rental property, and cannot pull a homeowner's permit if the property is not their primary residence.

The same section says a general contractor must be listed on the permit, and the City's pages do not say how the homeowner option applies to solar electrical work, so ask the Building Division before doing solar work yourself.
A building permit will not be issued to a homeowner for work performed by unlicensed contractors.
The City adopted the 2024 I-code package and the 2026 National Electrical Code with an effective date of August 1, 2026.
Plans must show fire setbacks of 18 inches from the ridge line and 36 inch pathways for each slope containing modules.
Electrical drawings must be stamped by a PE for PV systems of 10 kW DC or more.

The checklist's design criteria table lists a roof and ground snow load of 40 psf and a wind speed of 145 Vmph, while its structural plan requirements ask for a structural evaluation letter using a 30 lb/ft² snow load and VULT = 135 MPH, so confirm the design values with the Building Division.
Xcel Energy net metering: you must be an Xcel residential or business electricity customer, and the name on the application must match the name on the Xcel account or bill.

Xcel Energy net metering: the system must be sized so expected generation, combined with other distributed generation at the service address, does not exceed 200% of historical consumption (the previous 12 months at the time of application).
Xcel Energy net metering: all equipment must be UL 1741 SB certified and listed on the California Energy Commission Solar Equipment Lists.

eligibility_constraints.notes: License rules are from the City's Contractor License Information page, and homeowner rules from its Apply for Building Permits page. Conditions marked Xcel Energy are Xcel's and apply to Xcel customers.

value.name: Residential Solar PV building permit (Exhibit A flat fee)
value.notes: From Exhibit A of the City's Building Permit Fee Schedule, dated 1-1-26.

permit_fees.notes: The fee schedule says all fees are subject to change without notice. The schedule lists a plan check fee of 65% of the building permit fee. The schedule does not list Solar PV as exempt from the plan check fee, and it does not say whether that fee is added to the $100.00 Solar PV fee, so ask the Building Division. The schedule lists City use tax at 3.87% of 60% of total value (.02322 x value) and County use tax at 1.335% of 60% of total value (.00801 x value). Reinspection fees are $75.00 per hour, and electrical reinspection fees are $75.00 per inspection. The Inspections page says a Re-inspection Fee of $75 may be charged if the permit card or approved stamped plans are not on site. Work without an issued permit is charged double the building permit fee. Payment is due when permits are issued, by check, cash or credit card (Visa or Mastercard only).

value.name: Solar*Rewards Income Qualified upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says customers who qualify under the terms of Income Qualified can receive an upfront rebate of $3 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer and qualify under Xcel's Income Qualified terms.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Disproportionately Impacted Communities upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says Disproportionately Impacted Communities can receive an upfront rebate of $0.50 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer. The rebate is for Disproportionately Impacted Communities.

value.name: Switch Together Boulder County (group buying, not a rebate)
value.description: The City's Energy page describes Switch Together Boulder County as a group buying program for solar and batteries, formerly known as the Boulder County Solar Co-op.
value.eligibility: The program is open to anyone in Boulder County.

value.name: SolSmart installer discount
value.description: The City's Energy page says Lafayette received a Gold designation from the national SolSmart Program, and residents are eligible for a $500 discount from participating solar installers as a result. The page gives no date and does not list the participating installers.
value.eligibility: Lafayette residents using a participating solar installer.

rebates.notes: The Solar*Rewards rebates are Xcel Energy programs. Xcel's page says that as of 10/05/2026 it moved $1,050,000 from Solar*Rewards C&I to the Solar*Rewards Residential IQ/DIC program. The City's Energy page says Boulder County's EnergySmart offers residents a range of energy efficiency and solar rebates and financing, and free solar advising. The City's pages describe no City-funded rebate for residential solar.
